steps.prompt:
INTEGRATION STEP for Product Oracle v1. Read docs/v1-plan.md in full first. Lanes A (members), B2a/B2b (connectors) are already on main. The other lanes' work is on branches of origin: lane/k-connections, lane/b1-sources, lane/c-baseline, lane/f-templates, lane/d1-mcp, lane/d2-mcp-oauth, lane/e-runs (fetch them with git fetch origin 'refs/heads/lane/*:refs/remotes/origin/lane/*'). Each was built in parallel from an older main, and none was tested together.

1. Merge them into this branch in this order: k-connections, b1-sources, c-baseline, f-templates, d1-mcp, d2-mcp-oauth, e-runs. Resolve every conflict by keeping both lanes' intent: route registration in api/oracle/main.py, the generated web/lib/api (regenerate with `make openapi`, never hand-merge it), shared web navigation and components, and any duplicated helpers (B1 and K both read connection credentials: keep K's connections.service.get_credential and make B1 call it). Migrations: 0001-0003 on main, 0004 from d2-mcp-oauth; there must be one linear chain.
2. Wire the lanes together where each one left a hook: register D2's OAuth access-token verifier with D1's oracle.mcp.auth registry; make D1's curated search tool return B1's confidence; make E's runs ingest a segment's baseline.yaml artifact through C's YAML import (locks respected, proposals created); make F's priorities read C's evidence confidence.
3. Run everything: the full API suite against Postgres (ORACLE_TEST_DATABASE_URL), ruff check and ruff format --check, `make openapi` (commit the result), web lint, tsc, build, the Playwright mock suite, and `make e2e` if Postgres and Chromium are available. Fix what fails. If Chromium cannot start here, say so plainly; CI runs it.
4. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/integrate-report.md: conflicts and how each was resolved, wiring done, test results with counts, anything not verified.
Product Oracle words only: one company's Oracle, its users and their roles; never 'workspace'. Never touch .github/. Commit your work.

Decisions to apply while integrating (owner and engineering defaults, 2026-10-17): (a) API tokens can act for a user: migration 0005 (down_revision 0004) adds a nullable api_tokens.user_id FK; a token with a user acts as that user (role and owner) so `oracle sync` and other per-user calls work with ORACLE_API_TOKEN; tokens without a user keep today's behaviour. (b) When a sync gets a rejected credential, also mark the user's connection expired with last_error, so Settings > Connections shows Reconnect. (c) Disconnect also revokes the token at the provider where an endpoint exists (GitHub, Slack, Google), best effort, then deletes Oracle's copy. (d) Keep as built: a run's budget gates only the estimate; an MCP client asking for no scope gets oracle:read oracle:write (capped by the user's role); a run paused on overrun lets the running segment finish and keeps its output; immaterial conflicts apply as agent writes (locked items become proposals); OAuth registration stays open; grants slide 30 days; a resumed run gets 0.5x the estimate more; snapshots pin at start. (e) Do not spend effort on Lane K's per-user Claude plan or llm gateway: a later step removes them (agents and model calls run in SwarmCloud).

PUBLIC-LINK EVIDENCE for Product Oracle v1 (owner's decision, 2026-10-17: 'commenters can attach evidence or supporting docs in the UI via public links like public Notion pages or public Google Docs but will not need to connect their accounts'). Read docs/v1-plan.md (Amendments, Confidence) and the baseline code (api/oracle/baseline/, evidence model, confidence scoring) first.

Build: (1) POST /v1/baseline/evidence/link {target entity or edge, url, note?} for commenter and up: accept only https URLs of public pages (public Notion pages on notion.site or notion.so, Google Docs shared as 'anyone with the link', and plain public web pages); fetch server-side without any credential, with a timeout, size cap, content-type check and SSRF protection (resolve the host and refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses; no redirects to them); extract readable text (Google Docs via the public export ?format=txt endpoint; Notion public pages via their HTML; others via the page's main text), store a snapshot (title, text, fetched_at, last-modified when the page states it) and the evidence row with url, excerpt and kind so confidence scores it like a notion / google_docs / web source (freshness from last-modified, else fetched_at). A page that needs sign-in or is not public gets a clear 'this link is not public' error. Public-link evidence is visible to every user (it is public), unlike items from private connections. (2) Re-fetch on demand (POST .../refresh) to update the snapshot and rescore. (3) UI: on the Baseline feature drawer and on document sections, an 'Add evidence link' control for commenters and up, showing the fetched title, excerpt and confidence before saving. (4) Tests: allowed and refused URLs, SSRF refusal, non-public page, Google Docs and Notion extraction from recorded fixtures, scoring, role checks, Playwright mock test. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/public-links-report.md. Product Oracle words only; never touch .github/.

AGENTS RUN IN SWARMCLOUD for Product Oracle v1 (owner, 2026-10-17: 'product oracle orchestrates all its agents in swarmcloud, not in its own environment or separate runtimes, most work is done via these orchestrated agents that will use the LLM providers in SwarmCloud'). Read docs/v1-plan.md ('Agents and model calls' and 'Boundary with SwarmCloud') and docs/questions.md row P3b first.

Make the code match: (1) Remove Oracle's own model runtime: delete api/oracle/llm/ (Lane K's gateway that ran Claude Code or the Messages API inside Oracle), the Claude plan card and default-plan setting on Settings > Connections, the 'claude' provider from oracle.connections.providers, and the default_claude_connection_id company setting; migration 0006 (down_revision 0005) drops 'claude' from the connections provider check after deleting any claude rows, and the Dockerfile loses whatever Lane K added only for the headless Claude path. Data connections (GitHub, Slack, Notion, Fireflies, Google) stay exactly as they are. (2) Runs use SwarmCloud by default: ORACLE_RUNTIME defaults to 'swarmcloud'; FakeRuntime stays for tests and is chosen explicitly there; the UI and run notes say runs execute in SwarmCloud and use SwarmCloud's model accounts; until SwarmCloud #1433 lands, a run's notes still say agents cannot reach Oracle's data. (3) Any other place where Oracle wants model output (for example a summary) goes through one helper that dispatches a short SwarmCloud task via the runtime adapter and returns its artifact, never a local model call; if nothing calls it yet, add the helper with a test and no callers. (4) Tests: nothing in api/ imports anthropic, claude_agent_sdk or runs a claude binary (a test asserts this); runtime default; migration 0006 up/down; Connections page without the Claude card. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright mock tests. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/swarmcloud-agents-report.md. Product Oracle words only; never touch .github/.
